## The species registry: names, phases and per-species data (`species`) {#sec-ch02-species-registry}

### Summary

Every kintera module refers to species by position in one list. That list, with each species' phase, molar mass and
constant thermodynamic data, is read once from the `species` block of the YAML file into a process-wide registry.
The thermodynamics and kinetics options then copy the entries they need. A second YAML file with a different
`species` block refills the registry, so two configurations in one process each see their own species.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** One table of species: name, phase, molar mass, `cv_R`[^rg-69a0a493850f], `u0_R`[^rg-fa067cae2716], `s0_R`, NASA-9 coefficients.

**Data.** YAML `species` list in; global vectors indexed by species position out; molar mass in kg mol$^{-1}$.

**Placement.** Filled when options are read from YAML (`ThermoOptions.from_yaml`, `KineticsOptions.from_yaml`).

**Activation.** The `species` block is required; `phase` is optional (`gas`, `liquid`, `solid`).

**Guarantee / limits.** Card values stored as read, defaults filled; a failed load leaves an empty registry.

**Evidence.** See the Tests layer.
:::

Local symbols: $\mu_n$, molar mass of species $n$ [kg mol$^{-1}$]; $c^{\star}_n$, $u^{\star}_n$, $s^{\star}_n$ as
in the notation table (@sec-appa), the YAML keys `cv_R` [-], `u0_R` [K] and `s0_R` [-].

### Derivation

None: the registry stores data and derives nothing except the molar mass, which @sec-ch02-molar-mass gives. Each
species entry yields one row:

| YAML key | registry entry | default when omitted |
|---|---|---|
| `name`[^rg-e6bf2057e7b8] | `species_names` | required |
| `phase` | `species_phases` | empty (phase inferred from reactions) |
| `composition` | `species_weights`, through $\mu_n$ | required |
| `cv_R` | `species_cref_R` | $5/2$ |
| `u0_R` | `species_uref_R` | 0 |
| `s0_R` | `species_sref_R` | 0 |
| (name lookup) | `species_nasa9_low`, `species_nasa9_high`, `species_nasa9_Tmid` | zeros, 1000 K |

: Registry entries filled from one YAML species item. {#tbl-ch02-species-registry-entries}

The rows are read in `init_species_from_yaml`
({{< code src/species.cpp init_species_from_yaml overload=2 >}}). The default $c^{\star}_n = 5/2$ is $c_v/\mathcal R$ of a
diatomic ideal gas with frozen vibration (a monatomic gas has 3/2). The same default applies to condensates unless
`cv_R` is given (verified by reading the reader at the pin). All values are per mole: $\mu_n$ in kg mol$^{-1}$,
$c^{\star}_n$ and $s^{\star}_n$ dimensionless (divided by $\mathcal R$), $u^{\star}_n$ in K (energy per mole divided by
$\mathcal R$).

The registry holds every species of the card, but `ThermoOptions.from_yaml`
({{< code src/thermo/thermo_options.cpp ThermoOptionsImpl::from_yaml overload=2 >}}) copies only some of them: the
first species of the card, every species of a `nucleation`, `coagulation` or `evaporation` reaction, and every species
with an explicit `phase` (verified by reading at the pin). A species with no `phase` that appears in none of those
reactions is in the registry but not in the thermodynamics; for example the `H2O(s)` and `NH3(l)` entries of
`tests/jupiter.yaml`.

### Numerical method

No numerical method. The procedure is:

1. `ensure_species_initialized` ({{< code src/species.cpp ensure_species_initialized overload=2 >}}) compares the
   card's `species` block, dumped to text, with the block that filled the registry; if they differ or the
   registry is empty it reloads.
2. `init_species_from_yaml` clears the registry, then appends one row per species, checking the phase string.
3. Only after every species is read does it record the block and mark the registry initialised. On any exception
   it clears the registry and rethrows, so a failed card leaves neither partial data nor a cache hit.

The registry figure is not provided: the figure module is not written yet.

| what | code link | symbol | switch |

| reader | {{< code src/species.cpp init_species_from_yaml overload=2 >}} | `init_species_from_yaml` | `species` |
| reload test | {{< code src/species.cpp ensure_species_initialized overload=2 >}} | `ensure_species_initialized` | `species` |
| reset | {{< code src/species.cpp clear_species_registry >}} | `clear_species_registry` | always |
| per-options copy | {{< code src/species.hpp SpeciesThermoImpl >}} | `SpeciesThermoImpl` | API |

: Code map of the species registry. {#tbl-ch02-species-registry-code}

Setup checks a user can hit: a file without `species` is refused ("'species' is not defined"); a `phase` other than
`gas`, `liquid` or `solid` is refused.

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_species.release` (`SpeciesInit.clear_invalidates_success_and_same_card_reloads`) | clearing empties the registry; the same card reloads | exact | equality |
| `test_species.release` (`SpeciesInit.failed_parse_clears_partial_state_and_never_caches_success`) | a bad card leaves the registry empty and uninitialised | exact | equality |
| `test_species_registry.py` | a second card uses its own molar masses and species | $10^{-12}$ rel. | not yet derived |

: Tests of the species registry. {#tbl-ch02-species-registry-tests}

The tolerances are read from the test files at the pin. `test_species_registry.py` also has CUDA variants that
run when a GPU is present.

### Limits

The registry is process-wide state: two configurations used alternately in one process reload it on every switch.
No lock guards the registry vectors (verified by reading); that concurrent loading from several threads can corrupt
them is a hypothesis, not run. A species left out of `ThermoOptions` by the selection rule above is silently ignored by
the thermodynamics; no warning is printed.
